additions.name: Wingu Africa Mbezi Data Centre — Tanzania Phase 2 expansion (data hall under construction)
additions.site_identity_review: The Atlas site 'Wingu Africa Mbezi Data Centre, Dar es Salaam' (vcc-site-c02d5867672125f7e333) holds one project, curated:wingu-africa-mbezi-dar-es-salaam:operating-facility (operational, 12 August 2026). Wingu describes a single Tanzania facility: its Tanzania page speaks of 'Wingu Africa's Tanzania data centre' and of the TISPA exchange extended 'to our Mbezi data centre', and names no other Tanzanian facility; its 12 August 2026 announcement says it 'operates a carrier-neutral data centre in Dar es Salaam', with exchange connectivity 'extended to its Mbezi data centre', and that in March 2025 it 'launched the second phase of its Dar es Salaam data centre expansion'; its 18 March 2025 announcement calls Phase 2 'the second phase of its facility expansion', following 'Phase 1, introduced in 2022', adding white space and meet-me rooms to 'the facility'. The 3 November 2026 announcement certifies the design of 'its Tanzania data centre Phase 2 expansion in Dar es Salaam' (the 'Phase 2 data hall and designated meet-me rooms'). Phase 2 is therefore an expansion phase of the existing Mbezi data centre and belongs on this site. This is an identity inference from Wingu's single-facility statements; no Wingu plan or plot record separately locates the Phase 2 hall. The operating Phase 1 facility stays its own project with its own status, as with the Teraco CT1 expansion.

status.summary: Wingu Africa's announcement of 3 November 2026 says Uptime Institute has issued Tier III Certification of Design Documents for its Tanzania data centre Phase 2 expansion in Dar es Salaam, covering a stated peak IT load of 507 kW across the Phase 2 data hall and designated meet-me rooms, and that the Phase 2 expansion is 'currently under construction'. This records the Phase 2 expansion as under construction on 3 November 2026, the announcement day. It is not a construction start date (Wingu dates the launch of the second phase to March 2025); design certification is not completion, and the 507 kW is a design figure, not capacity in service.

locator.identity_review: Reuses the existing Mbezi campus point exactly (-6.7160669, 39.2018546; geometry evidence 0fb8883d-11b6-5ed5-8e9e-6527c58a7771 of project 4f99e7c8-464e-5384-b9c8-0b9470556f66, campus_locator, no geometry-identity evidence rows). No new coordinate is introduced. That point is a map-service feature pending replacement (locator_replacement_pending hold from loc-8-p6: Wingu's contact page gives 'Mbezi Industrial Area Plot No. 57' and no open Tanzanian cadastral or address service was found); any later locator_correction of the site moves this project with it. The point locates the Mbezi facility, not the Phase 2 data hall itself.

status.summary: On 27 October 2026 a scoping report prepared for Macquarie Data Centres (part of Macquarie Technology Group) was published on the NSW Planning Portal requesting project-specific SEARs for the Macquarie Engineering and Technology Campus (State significant development SSD-151494240) at Lot 1 DP1318560, 2 Alma Road, Macquarie Park; the request form followed on 28 October. The proposal is demolition, a public park, and the construction, fit-out and 24/7 operation of a multi-storey (40-45 m) data centre of 200 MW IT with about 139 back-up generators, ancillary offices and a teaching facility run in partnership with Macquarie University (data centre GFA 37,013 m2; estimated cost about AUD 2 billion). This supports an announced project only: SEARs have not been issued, no EIS has been lodged and no consent, site work or operation exists.
